main.1: Figure 1. Regional photovoltaic yield gains over crystalline silicon (c-Si). a,b, Single-junction gains at equal installed capacity, mapped and plotted against annual global horizontal irradiance (GHI). c,d, Corresponding tandem gains at equal aperture area. Each scatter includes 369 modelling regions; colour indicates mean air temperature on a shared scale. Dashed lines show descriptive linear fits; r and ρ are Pearson and Spearman correlations with GHI. GHI-quartile distributions are provided in Figures S104–S106.
main.2: Figure 2. Operating mechanisms of single-junction substitution and tandem enhancement. a, Electrical baseline and Shapley contributions to specific-yield gains over c-Si; the inset magnifies the incidence-angle modifier (IAM) contribution. b, Aperture-area gains separated into rated capacity density and density-weighted operating response. Bars and markers show regional means; whiskers span spatial P10–P90 across 369 regions, not confidence intervals. c,d, Matched response controls for single junction and two-terminal tandem, respectively. Dots show regions; lines connect GHI-quartile means (93, 92, 92 and 92 regions). Each gain uses c-Si under the same response switches. Temperature off fixes cells at 25 °C; spectrum off uses the reference spectrum, retaining temperature-driven current mismatch. All three off disables temperature, spectrum and IAM, retaining the electrical/system baseline. These controls are model counterfactuals.
main.3: Figure 3. Geographic compensation requirements from a common model baseline. a, Baseline specific-yield gains over c-Si across 369 regions per technology. Rugs show regions, points means, thick segments spatial P10–P90 and thin segments ranges. Curves show peak-normalized densities; dashed markers indicate the respective parity requirements. b, Single-junction aperture-parity coverage at λ = 0, 0.5 and 1 (baseline, intermediate and target). Circles and diamonds mark 50% and 100% coverage. Density increases are relative to the single-junction baseline density. The thermal-response target is γ = −0.10% °C⁻¹, with spectral scale fixed at 1. c, Paired tandem baseline and target gains; the target combines γ = −0.20% °C⁻¹ with a 1.75-eV top bandgap. Filled/open target symbols indicate regions at or above/below capacity parity. λ indexes prescribed response states at fixed voltage and rated density, not a coupled device-development trajectory.
main.4: Figure 4. Regional competitiveness conditions and remaining cost gaps. a,b, Baseline cost–lifetime scenarios for single junction under capacity constraints and tandem under site-area constraints. Backgrounds identify the NPV-maximizing technology in more than half of 369 regions; hatching marks no majority. Solid/dashed curves require candidate NPV to match both fixed rivals and no build in at least 50%/all regions. Diamonds mark reference scenarios; 25* separates the project-end replacement discontinuity. c,d, Corresponding regional gaps: the smaller upfront-only cost reduction required by either perovskite technology to meet the same threshold. All 369 regions per constraint are ordered by gap; ties stack. Baseline winners retain their technology class; other regions within 5% are near-transition. Remaining regions are c-Si-dominant or entry-limited. The cutoff is descriptive (Figures S136 and S137). No policy is applied. Capacity/site electricity values are 0.04/0.08 USD kWh⁻¹ over 25 years. O&M and replacement expenditure remain fixed. Full response comparisons and cross-context phase diagrams appear in Figures S122–S125 and S130–S135.
main.5: Figure 5. Decision effects of operating-response improvements and baseline support. a, Baseline choices under capacity and site-area constraints; symbols mark General-support thresholds for initially nonviable capacity opportunities. b, Candidate-specific initial-cost reductions required for parity against fixed rivals and no build at the response endpoint (left), and endpoint-minus-baseline changes (right). Dots show 369 regions per group; black intervals/ticks indicate interquartile ranges/medians, including zeros. c, Signed discounted-generation contributions from entry, technology switching and unchanged choices, followed by their net sum. Choices maximize NPV. b,c independently improve one candidate’s response while holding rivals, costs, density and durability fixed. d, Original-baseline choices before and after 20% support; band width denotes region count, with 369 paired choices per diagram. General supports all technologies; New technology supports single junction and tandem. d is a separate policy comparison. Portfolios contain standardized 1-MWp or 1-ha opportunities over 25 years. SJ, single junction.

si.S34: Figure S34. Device costs and regional operating responses. a, Units where candidate NPV exceeds c-Si NPV and zero across 54 cases. Filled circles/open squares denote capacity/site area at 0.04/0.08 USD kWh⁻¹. b, Single-junction capacity cost ceilings with coupled lifetime, degradation and burn-in; CAPEX multipliers also scale O&M and replacement. Thin/dark lines show nine casewise unit medians/their median; shading spans the smallest P10 to largest P90 across cases. The separate 25-year endpoint excludes replacement. c, Choices for 729 device pairs using unit-mean yield ratios, valued in the spatial reference model; diamonds mark central devices. Each portfolio contains 369 standardized 1-MWp or 1-ha opportunities.
si.S36: Figure S36. Conditional cost–lifetime phase diagrams for Huaibei. a,b, Single-junction capacity/site-area scans; c,d, corresponding tandem scans. Colour identifies the NPV-maximizing technology or no build; diamonds mark candidate baselines. Rivals, degradation, burn-in, O&M and replacement unit expenditure remain fixed. The separate 25-year row excludes replacement before the common horizon. Capacity/site electricity values are 0.04/0.08 USD kWh⁻¹. Huaibei represents median c-Si specific yield; all-region results accompany the figure.
si.S37: Figure S37. Regional choices and competitive margins. a, Paired capacity/site-area choices at 369 study-unit anchors, valued at 0.04/0.08 USD kWh⁻¹. b, Initial-cost reductions needed by losing candidates to match the best rival or no build, with O&M and replacement expenditure fixed. Winners are excluded. c, Choices at matched electricity values; site packing is 0.65 and the charge is 25 USD m⁻². d, Losing candidates within 1%, 5% and 10% cost-reduction thresholds. Curves summarize fixed model regions, not sampling uncertainty or adoption. SJ, single junction; T, tandem.
si.S40: Figure S40. Independent scenarios for matching silicon generation. a, Relative capacity density and specific yield. Solid/dashed lines indicate aperture/capacity parity; filled symbols show baseline means with spatial P10–P90, and open symbols show 54 case means. The arrow changes density at fixed specific yield. b, Coverage across nine temperature-coefficient (γ) and spectral-multiplier settings (369 regions); orange marks baseline, grey dashes mark threshold extrema, and shading beyond +10% denotes extrapolation. c, Tandem start (−0.40% °C⁻¹, 1.60 eV; open) and target (−0.20% °C⁻¹, 1.75 eV; filled). Groups I–III distinguish positive targets, positive thermal/bandgap increments with nonpositive targets, and nonpositive thermal increments/targets. These are ideal, reference-matched responses.
si.S41: Figure S41. Economic preference over silicon under a conditional 2035 scenario. Preference requires NPV > max(c-Si NPV, 0) over 25 years. a, Outcomes for 54 cases and 369 units; black ticks indicate positive physical gains. b, Single-junction capacity preference with lifetime varying alone or jointly with degradation and burn-in. Lines aggregate 3,321 unit–response pairs; bands span nine response-specific proportions. The 25-year diamonds exclude replacement. c, Initial/replacement-cost reductions for parity. Bars show medians of 27 casewise unit medians; intervals span those medians. Values >100% exceed cost elimination; dashes denote no replacement cost. Costs use constant 2024 USD.
si.S42: Figure S42. Baseline technology choices and construction support under conditional 2035 commissioning. a, Unsupported choices; symbols mark General-support thresholds for initially nonviable capacity projects. b, Maximum unsupported NPV by province under capacity (left) and site-area (right) constraints: dots show units, boxes quartiles/medians and whiskers extrema. Other 18 includes Chongqing (195 units). c, Choice transitions at 20% support; circle area denotes unit count, with open circles for zero. Each matrix totals 369. d, New capacity projects and site-area discounted-generation gains versus public cost at 0–30% support. Matched-gap support reproduces General choices using known financing gaps. Portfolios contain one 1-MWp or 1-ha opportunity per unit over 25 years; costs include 5% administration in constant 2024 USD. SJ, single junction; T, tandem.
si.S43: Figure S43. Continuous parameter paths from each technology’s primary-model baseline. a, Single-junction density requirements for 50% and 100% coverage at 11 states. b, Tandem specific-yield gains over the same c-Si comparator across 369 regions. Thin/blue curves show regional responses/their unweighted mean; shading spans spatial P10–P90, not confidence intervals. Rated density remains fixed. λ indexes parameter states rather than development time; mean response can decline between states.
si.S44: Figure S44. Full response comparison and paired changes in initial-cost thresholds. a–d, Baseline and target thresholds for single-junction capacity, single-junction site area, tandem capacity and tandem site area, respectively. e–h, Target-minus-baseline changes for the same four comparisons, using panel-specific linear scales. Solid/dashed lines require at least 50%/all of 369 regions. Thresholds match or exceed the NPV of both fixed rivals and no build, including ties. Only candidate operating response changes between paired states. All 656 absolute values and 328 paired differences are retained, including negative absolute thresholds that remain infeasible at nonnegative initial cost. Separate 25* strips preserve the project-end replacement discontinuity. Positive differences permit higher initial cost at the same coverage but do not establish absolute feasibility or actual adoption.
si.S45: Figure S45. Cross-context cost–lifetime conditions for regional technology choice. a, Single junction under site-area constraints; b, tandem under capacity constraints. Backgrounds identify the baseline NPV-maximizing choice in more than half of 369 regions; hatched Mixed zones have no majority. No build remains eligible. Solid/dashed curves require candidate NPV at least as high as both fixed rivals and zero in at least 50%/all regions, including ties. Diamonds mark baseline scenarios. Separate 25* strips preserve the project-end replacement discontinuity. Candidate initial cost and service life vary independently, with operating response, rival technologies, absolute O&M and replacement unit expenditure fixed. The horizon is 25 years; capacity/site electricity values are 0.04/0.08 USD kWh⁻¹, with a 25 USD m⁻² common site charge. Negative thresholds remain in source data but cannot be reached with nonnegative initial cost.
